<!-- FORGE:INVESTIGATOR -->
## Investigation Report

### Verdict / Confidence / Severity / Task Type
| Field | Finding |
| --- | --- |
| Verdict | Confirmed |
| Confidence | High |
| Severity | High |
| Task Type | Correctness / runtime integration bug |

### What Was Claimed
Read-only ForgeDock agents can successfully produce trusted zero-edit results, but pi-subagents applies the implementation no-edit completion guard and reports them as failed. The guard must remain enabled for implementation writers and be disabled for read-only roles.

### What We Found
The frozen integration base `staging` at `1e2a635ff05080dda36c17efe409e86af4fe17c4` registers `forge-review-correctness` and `forge-review-security` with `acceptanceRole: read-only` while also setting `completionGuard: true`. The runtime materializer emits `completionGuard: true` unconditionally, so generated read-only agent definitions cannot express their least-authority completion contract. The `forge-work-on` writer remains the only implementation-capable role in this base and must continue to require the guard.

### Root Cause
Completion-guard policy is encoded as a global materialization default and is enabled on read-only registrations. A successful zero-edit structured result therefore conflicts with the provider's implementation completion check even though the durable Forge result is valid.

### Affected Files
- `src/agents/register.ts` — read-only reviewer definitions incorrectly enable the guard.
- `src/agents/materialize.ts` — generated agent front matter hardcodes the guard instead of accepting a role-specific value.
- `test/adapters/subagents.test.ts` — runtime materialization needs a regression assertion for read-only false versus writer true.

### Evidence
- The registered reviewer definitions pair `acceptanceRole: read-only` with `completionGuard: true`.
- `agentFile` always renders `completionGuard: true`, regardless of role.
- The existing materialization test verifies hierarchy but does not verify completion-guard semantics.
- The writer `forge-work-on` definition has source-edit capabilities and must retain `completionGuard: true`.

### History Findings
Closed issue #49 and merged PR #57 documented the same false no-edit failure, but the tracked fix was associated with another integration branch. This issue remains a separate shipping/consumer-branch follow-up rather than a reason to skip the guarded change.

### Recommendation
Make completionGuard an explicit input to `agentFile`; pass `false` for every read-only reviewer and `true` for the writer in both runtime registration and materialization. Add a regression test that reads generated definitions and asserts the role-specific values.

### Related Issues
- #49 — closed predecessor for the same failure mode; not an active duplicate because its fix targeted a different branch.
- #57 — merged implementation of #49 on the other branch; reference only.

### Decomposition Assessment
No decomposition is required. The bounded change is a role-specific runtime configuration fix with a focused materialization regression test.

### Acceptance Spec
- Read-only reviewer definitions complete zero-edit structured results without an implementation completion guard.
- The implementation writer retains `completionGuard: true`.
- Generated agent files match the registration policy.
- Existing nested-review and runtime-isolation behavior remains unchanged.

<!-- INVESTIGATION:COMPLETE -->

<!-- FORGE:CONTRACT -->
## Builder Contract

### Objective
Make completionGuard an explicit role-specific runtime setting so read-only ForgeDock agents can complete valid zero-edit results while implementation writers retain no-edit enforcement.

### Allowed Paths
- `src/agents/register.ts`
- `src/agents/materialize.ts`
- `test/adapters/subagents.test.ts`

### Deliverables
1. Set `completionGuard: false` on read-only correctness and security registrations.
2. Set `completionGuard: true` explicitly on the writer registration.
3. Pass an explicit completionGuard value through `agentFile` and all materialized role definitions.
4. Add regression coverage for generated read-only and writer front matter.

### Invariants
- The `forge-work-on` implementation role remains a writer with `completionGuard: true`.
- Read-only reviewer tools, nesting limits, prompts, and extensions remain unchanged.
- No generated `.pi` runtime files or `.forge` policy files enter the source commit.
- The change does not weaken checkpoint, review, lease, or GitHub authority boundaries.

### Forbidden Changes
- Do not alter issue state, labels, comments, PRs, branches, or integration policy.
- Do not add role-specific bypasses outside the explicit acceptance-role contract.
- Do not remove the completion guard from implementation/remediation writers.
- Do not broaden the test or source scope beyond the three allowed paths.

### Acceptance Mapping
| Check | Implementation |
| --- | --- |
| Read-only completion is unguarded | Set false in read-only registrations and generated reviewer definitions. |
| Writer completion remains guarded | Set true in the writer registration and generated writer definition. |
| Runtime output is covered | Assert generated front matter in `test/adapters/subagents.test.ts`. |

<!-- FORGE:CONTEXT -->
## Implementation Context

The frozen base uses `registerForgeAgents` for in-process agent registration and `materializeForgeAgents` for generated `.pi/agents/*.md` definitions. The latter's `agentFile` helper currently hardcodes `completionGuard: true`, so it must receive a boolean input. The current test already materializes a writer and a read-only reviewer in a temporary repository, making it the narrowest regression surface.

<!-- FORGE:CONTEXT:COMPLETE -->
<!-- FORGE:ARCHITECT -->
## Implementation Plan

1. Extend the private `agentFile` input with `completionGuard: boolean` and render that value.
2. Pass `true` for `forge-work-on` and `false` for `forge-review-correctness` and `forge-review-security`.
3. Mirror the same explicit values in `registerForgeAgents` so runtime registration and materialized definitions agree.
4. Assert the generated writer and reviewer front matter contain the expected role and guard values.
5. Run the configured verification command(s) through `forge_verify`, then commit only the allowed source/test changes.

<!-- FORGE:ARCHITECT:COMPLETE -->
